verdict.rationale: AMD does publish a product spec page for the 9950X3D with concrete fields such as ECC support, NVMe RAID modes, supported OSes, 16 cores and up to 208MB of on-chip cache, so a real spec sheet exists. But the evidence shows none of the specific figures the story asks for: no clock speeds, power/TDP, memory speed support or AI TOPS, and no test conditions. Much of the surrounding page is marketing language. Missing for 10: base/boost clock figures, TDP/power ratings, supported memory speeds and capacity, AI TOPS figures, test-condition footnotes, and independent confirmation of the spec sheet's completeness.

support.subject: As a power-user, I can comparison-shop from a real spec sheet — the vendor publishes clocks, power, memory support, and AI TOPS with test conditions, instead of marketing adjectives
